key_insight: BT-QAOA approximates Max-k-Cut through binary-tree partitioning with standard MaxCut QAOA, reducing per-circuit resource demands without directly encoding k assignments per vertex.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make multiway graph-partitioning optimization more accessible on qubit- and gate-limited quantum hardware.
method: Run standard MaxCut QAOA on the full vertex set.
Repeatedly split the subset with the largest estimated cut-value gain, using at most 2k−3 MaxCut subproblems overall.
After k−1 splits, use the tree’s k leaves as the partition.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations report lower per-circuit qubit and gate overhead, high approximation ratios, and orders-of-magnitude improvements in estimated single-compiled-circuit success probability.
watch_item: Per-circuit savings require multiple subproblem solves; the abstract does not establish end-to-end runtime gains or hardware-validated performance.
paper_title: Binary-Tree Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for the Maximum $k$-Cut Problem
